Field Notes

What I learned shipping a tiny app

Small scope, real users, and the bugs nobody warned me about

Priya Raman
Feb 11, 2026

Last year I built an app that does one thing: it reminds you to water your plants based on the weather. I expected the hard part to be the code. It wasn't.

The hard part was deciding what not to build. Every week someone asked for a feature that would have made the app twice as big and only slightly more useful.

Thanks for reading Field Notes! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

Real users find real bugs

Within a day of launch, someone in Melbourne got a watering reminder at three in the morning. Time zones, as usual. I had tested in one city and assumed the rest of the world would behave.

The fix took ten minutes. Finding it took a stranger with a confusing email and a lot of patience.

Scope is a feature

People who use the app most say the same thing: it does one job and gets out of the way. That is the part I almost gave up first.
